title: IDF Strike Kills Hamas Finance Chief Muhammad Abu Alwan and Osama Abu Khater in Khan Younis
detail: A joint IDF and Israel Security Agency (Shin Bet) strike hit a vehicle in the Al-Mawasi area of western Khan Younis, southern Gaza, on September 23, 2026, killing 33-year-old Mohammad Ibrahim Mohammad Abu Alwan, a Rafah resident, and Osama Khaled Mohammad Abu Khater, of Bani Suheila; two more were wounded. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz said in a joint statement, 'A short while ago in Khan Younis, the IDF eliminated Hamas terrorist organisation finance department head Muhammad Abu Alwan,' calling him the group's senior financial official. Palestinian medics identified the two dead by name; no evidence was publicly presented for the militant designation.

media.caption: Palestinians inspect a vehicle struck by an Israeli strike in Khan Younis, Gaza, Sep 23, 2026

title: Separate Israeli Strikes Kill Two More Palestinians in Gaza City and Deir al-Balah
detail: Alongside the Khan Younis strike that killed Muhammad Abu Alwan and Osama Abu Khater, Israeli forces carried out at least two more deadly strikes on September 23, 2026: an aerial attack on a vehicle in Deir al-Balah, central Gaza, killed at least one Palestinian, and a separate strike in Gaza City killed at least one more. Al Jazeera put the day's overall toll across Gaza at seven killed, including two more who died of wounds sustained in earlier Israeli gunfire incidents.

title: Israeli Fire Kills Yahia Sammour in Khan Younis and Noura Diab in Bureij
detail: On the 349th consecutive day of reported ceasefire violations since the October 2025 truce, Israeli forces shot and killed Yahia Sammour in the as-Sater al-Gharbi area, north of Khan Younis, while tanks and helicopters shelled and fired on eastern Khan Younis and forces demolished homes in the northeastern part of the governorate. In central Gaza, Noura Awni Diab died of gunshot wounds sustained when Israeli forces shot her in the Al-Bureij refugee camp, where quadcopter drones and helicopters had been firing on homes. This report is currently sourced to a single outlet and has not yet been independently corroborated.

title: Board of Peace Unveils $2.45B, 66-Project Gaza Reconstruction Blueprint
detail: The US-backed Board of Peace unveiled a $2.45 billion, six-month blueprint covering 66 projects to begin rebuilding Gaza and restoring basic services, presented at a meeting in New York on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly on September 23, 2026. Reconstruction would proceed sector by sector, beginning in Rafah and moving northward, addressing infrastructure, education and healthcare. Medium-term reconstruction of Gaza's physical infrastructure is estimated at $35.2 billion, rising to $71.4 billion over a decade. Board high representative Nikolay Mladenov said progress hinges largely on Hamas disarmament, which the group has so far refused, adding 'we are not bound by a calendar.' Jared Kushner appealed for international support and ideas; no specific donor-country commitments were announced. On the ground, the Israeli military has expanded control to roughly 60% of Gaza, and the international stabilization force and new transitional governance body have not yet entered the territory — reconstruction has not begun.

media.caption: Board of Peace presents its Gaza reconstruction blueprint at the UN General Assembly, Sep 23, 2026
